cases.name: Eliza Nickole “Nicky” Almanza Morales
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Nicky’s zest for life was felt by all who knew her from the moment she was born. Her generous nature and kindheartedness will continue to be shown through her larger family and countless friends.

Growing up in the Chicagoland area, Nicky had come to love Mac Miller, Little Franks Pizza, Iced Coffee, and the outdoors, especially taking hikes with her two dogs. She shared these interests with her six sisters and dearest cousins, who she loved dearly and who love her continuously.

Nicky embarked on a career that was a true reflection of her compassionate nature. Nicky worked diligently for Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago, showing her lifelong commitment to helping those in need. Additionally, Nicky was an activist for women’s rights and the rights of those affected by war, famine, and domestic violence.

Nicky was married and had a beautiful one-year-old daughter, Zaila. Nicky loved being a mother, and Zaila was her pride and joy. Being a mother fulfilled Nicky, and she could not have been happier to welcome her next child, Xóchitl, into this world. The two of them now lie in peace together.

Nicky was a vibrant, passionate, and courageous person who will be missed by all those she knew and who knew her. We thank the Lord for the honor and privilege of having their beautiful souls in our lives. May she rest in eternal tranquility."
cases.narrative: He told police he was upset about the condition of a truck he bought from her husband and decided to take it out on her. He got into a fight with Morales, who told him she was pregnant, and stabbed her 70 times. He also stabbed the family dog, but the pet was able to escape and survive.
